patch_description: A fundamentally different approach: instead of sliding-window polynomial fitting, this uses a two-state Kalman filter (level + slope) with an adaptive process-noise scheduler driven by a trend-consistency detector. The Kalman filter inherently minimizes lag because it is predictive (the slope state carries the signal forward one step). Lag error is further canceled by running the filter forward, then re-running it backward over a short lookback window and fusing via weighted blend that is exact for linear trends (zero-lag for ramps). Slope-change spurious reversals are suppressed by the adaptive Q matrix: when the last K slope signs agree, process noise on the slope collapses, making the filter resist direction changes (smooth trends); when a persistent innovation (prediction error) exceeds a Mahalanobis threshold, Q is inflated so the filter snaps to genuine reversals quickly. This directly targets all four objectives with O(1) per-sample cost (no window refits), giving both low latency and low reversal count.
